about.zmksDescription: ZMKs Studio is a community build based on ZMK Studio. It keeps the upstream ZMK Studio keymap editing workflow and adds this fork's UI, lighting, localization, and desktop client improvements. The original ZMK Studio project and ZMK contributors remain the foundation of this work.
about.sponsorsDescription: ZMK Studio is made possible thanks to the generous donation of time from our contributors, as well as the financial sponsorship from the following vendors:

behaviorDesc.None: Block the key — events won't pass to layers below

behaviorDesc.To Layer: Switch to a layer and deactivate all others except default

flavorDesc.holdPreferred: Fires the hold as soon as the term passes or another key is pressed. Best for modifiers.
flavorDesc.balanced: If you press and release another key while holding, it resolves to a hold; release this key first and it taps. Fits how most modifiers are used.
flavorDesc.tapPreferred: Only holds if you truly keep it pressed past the term. Fewest typing misfires.
flavorDesc.tapUnlessInterrupted: Taps by default, holds only when interrupted by another key.

desc.retroTap: Held past the term without pressing another key? Still send the tap on release.
desc.holdWhileUndecided: Activate the hold immediately while deciding instead of waiting. Useful for mouse modifiers.
desc.holdWhileUndecidedLinger: Keep the hold active until just after the tap is sent. Only matters with Immediate Hold.
desc.holdTriggerOnRelease: Delay the positional hold decision until the key is released.
desc.quickTapMs: Press the key again within this time after a tap to tap again — e.g. tap-then-hold Backspace to repeat.
desc.requirePriorIdleMs: If you pressed another key within this time, resolve to a tap — avoids accidental holds while typing fast.

combos.editingBanner: Editing combo behavior — pick a binding, then confirm.
combos.saveFailed: Save failed or timed out. Please try again.
combos.timeoutDesc: How long all keys must be pressed within, in milliseconds.
combos.priorIdleDesc: Only trigger if no other key was tapped shortly before the combo's first key.
combos.slowReleaseDesc: Release the combo when the last key is released, instead of the first.
combos.layersDesc: Layers this combo is active on. With none selected, it works on every layer.
combos.triggerHint: Click keys on the layout to add or remove them from this combo.
combos.readOnlyHint: This firmware can't edit key positions or the behavior at runtime — change them in your keymap / devicetree.
combos.allReservedHint: Every combo slot on this keyboard is reserved by firmware. The unlock shortcut is managed from the Device page.
combos.clearFailed: Couldn't clear the slot. Please try again.

motion.emptyHint: No motion sensor was detected on this device, or the firmware has the motion subsystem disabled.

carry.title: Carry sleep
carry.desc: Sleeps on its own while it's being carried, and wakes when it's set down
carry.activeHint: Still moving — the keyboard will sleep now; set it down to wake it
carry.idleHint: Resting — carry it around and it will sleep on its own
carry.motionDurationHint: Movement must be this sustained before sleeping — a single jolt won't do it; a key press always cancels
carry.calibrateHint: Pick the keyboard up and walk a few steps to see the range the signal settles into, then set the motion threshold from the bottom of that range.

stillWake.title: Settle wake
stillWake.desc: Stays awake once the keyboard has been set down still
stillWake.settleDurationHint: After a motion wake-up the keyboard must stay this still, or it goes straight back to sleep — a bag keeps moving, a desk doesn't
stillWake.meterHint: The settle window only watches whether motion has fallen silent, so no threshold marker applies here.

tap.title: Case tap
tap.desc: Tap the case to trigger actions, one binding per side and tap style
tap.bindingTitle: Action triggered by this tap slot
tap.windowHint: When a single and a double share a side, the single fires this long late so the double can win
tap.layersHint: Taps only fire while one of these layers is active; leave all off for every layer
tap.allLayersOff: Leave all off for every layer
tap.calibrateHint: Tap the case and read the peak marker it leaves behind, then set the threshold just below it — too low and typing vibration will trigger it.

unlockPanel.title: Unlock shortcut
unlockPanel.desc: The keyboard locks itself so a web page can't change your keymap without you. Unlocking is always a physical action — Studio cannot do it remotely.
unlockPanel.protectedHint: Firmware reserves this slot for unlocking, so it can't be repointed at another behavior.
unlockPanel.noneDesc: This firmware exposes no studio unlock binding. Once the keyboard locks, Studio won't be able to edit it again — reflash before locking it.
unlockPanel.changeHint: You'll be asked to perform the new gesture before it replaces the current one, and the keyboard stays unlocked throughout.
unlockPanel.noSpareSlot: Setting up a combo shortcut needs one free combo slot to confirm the gesture with. Free a slot on the Combos page first.
unlockPanel.createHint: Sets up a key combination that unlocks the keyboard, alongside the existing unlock key. You'll be asked to perform it once before it's saved.

unlockChange.title: Change unlock shortcut
unlockChange.pickHint: Click the keys the shortcut should use — at least two, pressed together.
unlockChange.noLayout: No physical layout reported, so keys can't be picked.
unlockChange.warnConflict: Another combo already uses exactly these keys. Pick a different set.
unlockChange.warnTyping: These are all ordinary keys, so the chord could fire while typing. Studio will require a brief pause before it counts — including one layer or modifier key is safer.
unlockChange.pressHint: Your current shortcut is untouched until this one is confirmed, and the keyboard stays unlocked throughout — so nothing is at risk if it doesn't work.
unlockChange.confirmedHint: The keyboard produced the test keystroke, so this gesture works. Apply it as the unlock shortcut?
unlockChange.timeoutSafe: You can apply without confirmation; this keyboard still has another way to unlock.
unlockChange.timeoutRisky: Applying without confirmation means that if the gesture doesn't work, the keyboard can't be edited again without reflashing.
unlockChange.doneHint: It's live right now, but only in memory — write it to the keyboard or it's gone at the next power cycle.
unlockChange.priorIdleApplied: A brief pause is now required before the chord counts, so it can't fire while typing.
unlockChange.warnUnverified: Applied without confirmation — test it before you let the keyboard lock.
unlockChange.errArm: Couldn't set up the test. Nothing was changed.
unlockChange.errCommit: Writing the new shortcut failed. Your old one still works.
unlockChange.errNoKeyPress: This firmware has no Key Press behavior, so the gesture can't be tested.
unlockChange.timeoutNoInput: No keystrokes are reaching Studio at all. Make sure this window has focus and that the keyboard is typing into this computer.
unlockChange.tryAnotherProbe: Retry with a different test key
unlockChange.timeoutSwallowed: If pressing them together shows nothing at all, the combo IS firing — ZMK swallows the keys it consumes and sends the test key instead, so only the test key is going missing. Try a different one. (Seeing the keys individually just means the chord didn't complete.)
unlockChange.errStoredBehavior: Firmware accepted the test but didn't store the test keystroke on the slot. That's why the chord swallows keys and emits nothing — the trigger landed and the behavior didn't. This needs a firmware fix; the read-back above is the evidence.
unlockChange.errStoredPositions: Firmware accepted the test but stored different trigger keys, so this device isn't taking the write as sent.
unlockChange.pickHintCreate: Your existing unlock key stays as it is, so this is purely an addition.
unlockChange.warnOverlap: These keys are also used by another combo
unlockChange.warnOverlapHint: Overlapping combos compete, and the other one may win — which makes the test below look like it failed for no reason.
unlockChange.warnSameAsCurrent: That's the shortcut already in use, so there's nothing to confirm. Pick different keys — or cancel to keep it as it is.
unlockChange.warnShadowedByUnlock: These keys overlap your current unlock shortcut, which stays live during the test. It would win the chord and unlock instead of producing the test keystroke, so the test can't confirm anything. Pick keys it doesn't share.
unlockChange.savedOk: Written to the keyboard — firmware reports the shortcut on the slot.
unlockChange.savedVerifyHint: Studio can't see storage, only the live slot. Worth unplugging the keyboard and reconnecting once to confirm it stuck — while your old unlock method still works.
unlockChange.savedFailed: The save didn't take — firmware doesn't report the shortcut on the slot afterwards. Don't let this keyboard lock until you've used your existing unlock method to check it.

step.flashHint: A bare board already sits in the UF2 bootloader — plugging in is enough
step.deviceHint: Record model and serial, wait for re-enumeration
step.unlockHint: Shipping firmware is locked, so the unlock chord has to be pressed once
step.keysHint: Drag a squeegee across the board — all green passes it
step.imuHint: Pick it up, tilt and tap — the tool judges
step.rgbHint: Runs a colour sweep, confirmed by eye
step.finishHint: Discard test edits, re-lock, write the log

flash.title: Flash firmware
flash.subtitle: Plug the keyboard in over USB. A bare board stops in its UF2 bootloader on its own, so no key press is needed.
flash.desktopOnly: This is not the desktop client, so nothing can be written to a mass-storage volume.
flash.modelMismatch: Detected board does not match the configured model, writing disabled: detected
flash.noModelCheck: No expected model configured, so no model check is performed. Worth setting the Model keyword for the line.

device.title: Read device info
device.subtitle: The board reboots after flashing; the tool attaches on its own and reads the model and serial number.
device.hint: If the board is plugged in but never attaches: try another USB port, or confirm the firmware really is flashed — a board with no application firmware never presents a serial port.

unlock.title: Unlock keyboard
unlock.subtitle: Shipping firmware is locked, so Studio cannot read the keymap. Press the unlock chord — the tool notices on its own.
unlock.hint: That is the firmware's factory-default chord. If this unit uses a custom one, use yours — the tool only watches the lock state.
unlock.noConn: Not connected to a keyboard yet, go back a step.

keys.title: Full key scan
keys.subtitle: Drag a squeegee across the board from left to right and press every key. Keys turn green as they register; all green passes it — there is no button to press.
keys.precheckSubtitle: First confirm this computer receives the keyboard's keystrokes. Drag the squeegee across part of the board, or just press a few keys.
keys.precheckPlaceholder: Characters the keyboard types will appear here…
keys.skipPrecheck: Skip the check and scan anyway
keys.readbackMismatch: Firmware read back a different binding from the one written, so the test keymap never took effect — this one needs firmware-side confirmation.
keys.noInputSkipped: No keystroke arrived during the scan. The pre-check was skipped, so start by confirming this computer receives the keyboard's input.
keys.noInputAfterOk: The pre-check received keystrokes but the test keymap produced none, so the test keymap never took effect — the keyboard is not the problem. Worth reporting to whoever owns the firmware.
keys.noInputFail: No keystroke arrived, so nothing could be judged
keys.stallDetail: seconds without a new position answering, and not one key registered. Check the squeegee is really pressing the keys, then try again.
keys.noneSeen: Not one key position responded, so nothing could be judged
keys.unmatched: That keystroke belongs to no position in this sweep
keys.unmatchedHint: This sweep only covers the positions shown. Keystrokes from the bench PC's own keyboard do not count — use the squeegee on the keyboard itself.
keys.checkFocus: Click this window so it is the active one — keystrokes do not reach it while it is not focused.
keys.checkOutput: The keyboard's USB output may have been switched to Bluetooth: press the output-switch key to bring it back to USB.
keys.checkNotepad: Try typing into Notepad: if that does not type either, the problem is the keyboard or the cable, not this tool.
keys.noKeymap: Could not read the keymap (the keyboard may have re-locked)
keys.noBehaviors: Firmware is missing the Key Press / None behaviors

imu.title: IMU motion check
imu.subtitle: Pick the keyboard up, tilt it, then tap it twice. Any detected motion passes it — no specific gesture required.
imu.unsupported: This firmware has no motion subsystem, so the IMU cannot be checked. The step is recorded as SKIP, not as a pass.
imu.go: Pick it up and tilt / tap it now
imu.criteria: Any one of three signals passes it: peak over threshold, a change of orientation, or a detected tap.
imu.noData: No data arrived after enabling the live stream

rgb.title: RGB lighting check
rgb.subtitle: The tool walks the colour sequence; confirm by eye that each segment lights in the right colour.
rgb.unsupported: This firmware reports no RGB underglow. The step is recorded as SKIP, not as a pass.
rgb.watch: Watch the keyboard — note which segment does not light.
rgb.question: Did red, green, blue and white all light correctly?

finish.title: Wrap up
finish.subtitle: Test edits are never written to flash. This step only discards and re-locks, so the unit leaves in the state a customer receives.
finish.noConn: Not connected, skipping the wrap-up actions
finish.discardFailed: Could not discard edits (device may be gone)
finish.lockFailed: Lock did not take — confirm after a power cycle
finish.note: The log is stored on this machine. Unplug and pack it; if this unit failed, tag it and hand it to repair.
